global_cutaway.name: B
global_cutaway.rule: Lower only the true camera-facing south/front exterior shell. Rear walls and interior partitions remain architectural walls rather than being removed by a global depth slice.

bedroom_front_wall.name: C
bedroom_front_wall.rule: Preserve the desk-facing bedroom wall as a solid lower base plus a translucent upper wall so bedroom/bath separation remains legible while the desk and monitor can be read through it.
bedroom_front_wall.presentation_semantics: The translucent upper wall is a dashboard/dollhouse visibility treatment, not a claim that the real apartment has a glass wall.

projector_wall.rule: Keep the bedroom/living divider and projector wall as normal physical architecture. Do not delete it or invent a double-sided/fake projector screen solely to expose the bedroom-facing projection surface to the accepted camera.
projector_wall.active_projector_visual: deferred to live-state/lighting design after physical-world blocking acceptance

renderer_requirements: Preserve approved x/y wall geometry and aperture spans exactly.
Do not use image generation to reconstruct, reinterpret, or compare apartment geometry or camera visibility.
Render the floor as a guaranteed underlay so it cannot painter-sort over and visually erase wall faces.
Depth-sort wall caps with wall/object faces rather than painting caps as a final overlay.
The bedroom translucent upper wall must preserve the bedroom-door aperture rather than glazing across the opening.
Visibility treatments may alter presentation opacity/height only; they do not move rooms, walls, openings, or objects in x/y.
